liebermann.description_de: Londoner Guildhall, eine Hs. (dort mindestens 1639 bis 1721), von der jetzt nur die Varianten bekannt sind
liebermann.shelfmark_as_given: London, Guildhall (Corporation of London), a lost manuscript (there from at least 1639 to 1721), known only from the variants cited by earlier editors as “Lond”
liebermann.notes: A manuscript kept at the London Guildhall from at least 1639 to 1721, now known only from the variants the editors cited under the siglum 'Lond'; it had Hn and Hn Lond and belonged to the Lond class (Leges Anglorum Londoniis collectae), closest to Or. Spelman (Conc. I 34) collated Epist. Eleuth. from it and dated it 15th century; a reading at p. 570 shows it was not merely a modern copy.

entries.text_de: Mindestens von 1639 bis 1721 bewahrte die Londoner Guildhall eine Hs. von Hn, s. u. S. 547, mit Hn Lond, u. S. 524, von der jetzt nur die Varianten bekannt sind, welche die Editoren daraus unter der Sigle Lond notirt haben. Sie gehörte zur Classe Lond, d. h. den Leges Anglorum Londoniis s. XIII in. collectae (vgl. dort p. 104) und war Hs. Or nächst verwandt7. Sie könnte vielleicht nur eine moderne Abschrift scheinen, wenn sie nicht u. S. 57010 neben richtigem promoveri das falsche promereri nur als Schreibervorschlag böte, welches Lond's andere Codices allein haben. Spelman Conc. I 34 verglich aus Gi Epist. Eleuth., u. S. 636 [zu 637 Anmm. 8. 11 hatte Gi puerum . . dimicabunt]; nach ihm p. 36 war Gi 15. Jhs.
entries.text_en: From at least 1639 to 1721 the London Guildhall kept a MS of Hn, see below, p. 547, with Hn Lond, below, p. 524, of which now only the variants are known which the editors noted from it under the siglum Lond. It belonged to the class Lond, i.e. the Leges Anglorum Londoniis s. XIII in. collectae (cf. there p. 104), and was most closely related to MS Or7. It might perhaps seem to be merely a modern copy, were it not that below, p. 57010, beside the correct promoveri it offers the wrong promereri, only as a scribal suggestion, which Lond's other codices alone have. Spelman, Conc. I 34, collated Epist. Eleuth. from Gi, below, p. 636 [at 637 nn. 8. 11 Gi had puerum . . dimicabunt]; according to him, p. 36, Gi was of the 15th century.

transcription.doubts: '570<sup>10</sup>' is a page-and-note reference, not this page's note 10. 'Conc. I 34' confirmed. Note mark 7 stands after 'verwandt' (checked).
Cross-reference line only, printed centred like a heading; no body text.
